subject: MAP: POC peering fallback and org bootstrap plan
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta@clearbridge.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@atlashealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 May 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff and network questions for POC

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Atlas Health is ready to start a 4-week POC but we need the MAP (mutual action plan) to tie the activation milestones to our network windows. Two quick asks up front:

1) We require an explicit fallback for VPC peering if we can't complete peering within the first 7 days (our security team insists on a fallback to public endpoints and an IP allowlist).
2) We also need clear instructions for org onboarding and API key provisioning for a scoped evaluation org (we will create a staging org under atlas-eval).

Can you send a MAP that includes the peering fallback option, API key lifecycle, and IP allowlist steps? If you can include a suggested cutover schedule and one-hour maintenance windows for the peering handshake that would help our infra team plan.

Thanks — Marta
Marta Alvarez
Director, Cloud Ops
ClearBridge / Atlas Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@clearbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff and network questions for POC

Hi Marta — great to hear Atlas is ready. Attached is an initial MAP and a short network runbook snippet that maps to the four-week cadence. High level summary below and the attachment (MAP_Atlas-v1.pdf) contains the day-by-day checklist.

Summary (short):
- Week 0 (preflight, day -2 to day 0): org seed, service account creation, create atlas-eval org, add two admins, and generate initial API keys (ephemeral keys enabled).
- Week 1 (day 1–7): provisioning + IP allowlist + dry peering test (non-production traffic). If VPC peering completes in this window we move to warmup.
- Peering fallback: if peering cannot be established by day 7, we will follow the fallback plan — enable public-hosted endpoints behind strict IP allowlist for Atlas CIDR blocks and rotate ephemeral API keys every 7 days during the POC. This preserves security posture while removing the peering blocker.
- Week 2: warmup traffic + model validation + quality checks; we recommend a 30m ramp test each morning for three days.
- Week 3: performance tuning, batching profile and quantization suggestions (if requested).
- Week 4: acceptance window and handoff.

Action items for Atlas (what we need from you):
- Org seed UID and two admin emails for atlas-eval (send by EOD Monday)
- IP ranges to add to allowlist (CIDR blocks, preferred source ranges)
- Preferred peering maintenance windows (we suggest UTC 02:00–03:00 but can adjust)

I've attached network-runbook-snippet.md with the exact commands for VPC peering, the ephemeral-key-rotation.csv with an example rotation schedule, and the MAP_Atlas-v1.pdf with acceptance criteria. Ben and Neha are looped in for the peering and auth details.

I'll follow up to propose a one-hour window for the initial peering handshake once we get your CIDRs.

Best,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@clearbridge.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff and network questions for POC

Hi Marta — quick technical notes and a pragmatic fallback checklist I added into the runbook: 

1) VPC peering checklist (short): create peering request from Atlas VPC -> accept from Redwood console -> configure route tables -> test TCP/HTTPS to 10.x private endpoint -> validate MTU/path. Plan for 30–60 minutes in normal conditions; allow 4 hours in the rare case of cloud provider ticketing.
2) Fallback (public endpoint + IP allowlist): we will create a scoped TLS endpoint (client cert optional) and add Atlas CIDRs to the allowlist. We will also enable request-level origin validation and prefix KV caching to reduce token costs while on the public path.
3) API keys and org bootstrap: we recommend issuing ephemeral keys scoped to atlas-eval:env=staging with a 7-day TTL for the POC. We will provide an example CLI snippet in the runbook.

Quirks to watch for: if Atlas is using strict egress filtering, please ensure the following Redwood IPs are whitelisted for the handshake and for CRL/OCSP checks (listed in the runbook).

If you share the CIDRs and a preferred peering slot for Wednesday or Thursday this week we can reserve the window on our side.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Infrastructure Solutions | Redwood Inference
